label: Decision
summary: Each decision in the game's database.
details: It runs over the whole list of decision definitions. The game lists no surrounding scope for it, so it needs no character or title around it. The vanilla files do not use it.

label: Defended great holy war
summary: Each great holy war that the faith is defending against.
details: Works on a faith. The items are great holy wars (the large religious wars the game has between faiths). The vanilla files do not use it.

label: De jure vassal title holder
summary: Each character who holds a vassal title of the title, going by the de jure map (the intended borders).
details: Works on a title. The game's documentation calls them the vassal holders of the title. Vanilla uses it to change the liege of these holders, to reach their courtiers, and in the trigger form to check whether the diarch of some character is among them.

label: Desired tenet
summary: The tenets (core beliefs of a faith) that the character would pick for their own faith, best first.
details: Works on a character, and only looks at tenets that character knows. Tenets are ranked by how much they would raise the character's starting fulfillment (how satisfied the character is with the faith). By default only tenets with a positive effect count, and the number of tenets is limited by the game's core tenet cap. The game's documentation also names an `only_negative` option, but its own example and every vanilla use write `only_positive`. Vanilla often writes `selection_count = 97`, which is simply a high number.

fields.name: selection_count
fields.text: Keep only the best N tenets.

fields.name: only_positive
fields.text: Whether to leave out tenets that do not improve the character's starting fulfillment. Vanilla also sets it to no to get all tenets.

fields.name: threshold
fields.text: Only tenets whose fulfillment change is at least this value. It only has an effect when only_positive is yes.

label: Diarchy successor
summary: Each character in the line of succession of the diarchy of the scoped character.
details: Works on a character. If there is no active diarchy, or the active one has no succession, it goes through the regency candidates instead. Vanilla uses it to find vizier candidates, to rank successors with a script value, and to change opinions of those in line.

label: Diplomacy councillor
summary: Each councillor whose job is based on the diplomacy skill.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla uses the trigger form to check how many such councillors there are and how high their diplomacy is, and the random form to pick one and save it.

label: Direct de facto vassal title
summary: Each title that is a vassal title of the title in practice, as things stand now.
details: Works on a title. De facto means how things actually stand, as opposed to de jure (the intended map borders). Vanilla uses it to check a title's duchy and to pick one whose holder is someone other than the root character and save that holder.

label: Direct de jure vassal title
summary: Each title that lies directly below the title by the map's intended borders.
details: Works on a title: for an empire its kingdoms, for a kingdom its duchies, and so on. De jure means by the intended borders, regardless of who holds the land. Vanilla uses it to apply effects to each such title (for example county modifiers on its counties), to pick a random one and save it, and to count how many meet a condition.

label: Directly owned province
summary: Each province that the character holds directly.
details: Works on a character. Directly owned means the character's own provinces, not those held through their vassals. Vanilla uses it to add province modifiers, to find a province with a free building slot or a given holding type, and to check terrain and buildings.

label: Doctrine
summary: Each doctrine defined in the game.
details: Doctrines are the beliefs of a faith. It runs over all doctrine definitions, not just those a certain faith has, and needs no surrounding scope. Vanilla uses the trigger form once, with a custom check on each doctrine.

label: Domicile
summary: Each domicile in the game.
details: The game's documentation only says it goes through all domiciles and does not explain what one is. It needs no surrounding scope. Vanilla uses the every form with `limit` and `switch`, and once inside another `every_domicile`.

label: Duchy
summary: Each duchy title in the game.
details: It covers every duchy on the map, not only those of one realm, and needs no surrounding scope. Vanilla uses it to change a duchy's de jure liege (the title above it by the map) and to pick a duchy by its capital county.

label: Dynasty
summary: Each dynasty in the game.
details: Dynasties without a head are left out unless you add `include_inactive = yes`. It needs no surrounding scope. Vanilla uses it once, to go on into the houses of each dynasty.

fields.name: include_inactive
fields.text: Also go through dynasties that have no head.

label: House
summary: Each house that belongs to the dynasty.
details: Works on a dynasty. A house is a branch of a dynasty. Vanilla uses it once, to go on into the relations of each house.

label: Dynasty member
summary: Each character who belongs to the dynasty.
details: Works on a dynasty. Vanilla uses it to give opinions and traits to the whole dynasty, to collect candidates into lists, to rank members by a skill or age, and to pick one by condition.

label: Election candidate
summary: Each character who is a valid candidate in the election for the title.
details: Works on a title. Vanilla uses it to check whether a given person is among the candidates and to find the candidate a character has voted for.

label: Electable title
summary: Each title that the character is allowed to vote on.
details: Works on a character. The vanilla files do not use it.

label: Elector
summary: Each character who is a valid elector in the election for the title.
details: Works on a title. Vanilla uses it to pick the elector ordered first by intrigue, to pick a random voter, and to test electors for a murder plot.

label: Eminent holy site
summary: Each active eminent holy site of the faith.
details: Works on a faith. The game's documentation says it is the same as the holy site list filtered with `is_eminent = yes`; its sentence about the list size is cut off, so that part is unclear. Vanilla uses it to reach the holy site's county and to save a holy site for later.

label: Empire
summary: Each empire title in the game.
details: It covers every empire on the map and needs no surrounding scope. Vanilla uses it to set the de jure liege title of empires, to build a list for a decision, to pick a rival realm, and to filter by holder.

label: Entourage member
summary: Each character who travels along with the owner of the travel plan, including the travel leader but not the owner.
details: Works on a travel plan. Vanilla uses it a lot: to give opinions, to pick who is affected or who helps on a journey, to order members by a skill, and to check who is adult and available.

label: Epidemic
summary: Each epidemic in the world.
details: It needs no surrounding scope. Vanilla uses it to pick a random epidemic, to order them, and to check how intense an outbreak is.

label: Epidemic type
summary: Each epidemic type defined in the game.
details: It runs over the definitions (the kinds of epidemic), not over running epidemics, and needs no surrounding scope. The vanilla files do not use it.

label: Equipped artifact
summary: Each artifact the character currently has equipped.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla uses it to check the slot (such as armor, helmet, regalia or primary armament) or type (such as sword or axe) of what a character wears and to save one for later.

label: Extended family member
summary: Each person in the character's extended family.
details: Works on a character. The game's documentation names uncles and aunts, nephews and nieces, and cousins. Vanilla uses it to collect characters into a list.

label: Faction county
summary: Each county that is a member of the faction.
details: Works on a faction. This is for factions that counties join (vanilla uses it with peasant factions), not for those that characters join. Vanilla uses it to change county control (how firmly the holder controls the county), add county modifiers, and save counties.

label: Faction member
summary: Each character who is a member of the faction.
details: Works on a faction. Vanilla uses it to send events, change opinions, add truces both ways, and make members change liege or become independent. For county members, use the faction county list.

label: Faith
summary: Each faith that belongs to the religion.
details: Works on a religion. Vanilla uses it to change fervor (a faith's religious zeal), add doctrines, and go through the rites and rulers of each faith.

label: Faith follower
summary: Each character who follows the faith.
details: Works on a faith. Vanilla uses it to send events, change the characters' faith, pick one at random, and to check conditions like piety level or prowess.

label: Faith county
summary: Each county of the faith.
details: Works on a faith. The vanilla files only use the random form.

label: Faith duchy
summary: Each duchy that has at least one county of the faith.
details: Works on a faith. The duchy does not have to be fully of that faith. The vanilla files do not use it.

label: Faith empire
summary: Each empire that has at least one county of the faith.
details: Works on a faith. The empire does not have to be fully of that faith. The vanilla files do not use it.

label: Faith hegemony
summary: Each hegemony that has at least one county of the faith.
details: Works on a faith. The input does not explain what a hegemony is. The vanilla files do not use it.

label: Holy order
summary: Each holy order of the faith.
details: Works on a faith. Vanilla uses it to find the order that fits a condition (its leader, patron or title) and to send events.

label: Faith kingdom
summary: Each kingdom that has at least one county of the faith.
details: Works on a faith. The kingdom does not have to be fully of that faith. The vanilla files do not use it.

label: Playable ruler of the faith
summary: Each playable ruler who follows the faith.
details: Works on a faith. Vanilla uses it to send events, to add rulers to a list, and to check conditions.

label: Rite
summary: Each rite of the faith.
details: Works on a faith. Vanilla uses it to change a rite's doctrines, set its parent faith, set whether it can be converted to, make a rite the main one, and to order rites by their converted development or county count.

label: Ruler of the faith
summary: Each ruler who follows the faith.
details: Works on a faith. The game has a separate list of playable rulers of the faith, and the input does not say how the two differ.

label: Religious subordinate
summary: Each member of the faith's religious hierarchy below the head of faith, at any level.
details: Works on a faith. The head of faith is left out. Challengers (antipopes) count as subordinates of the top superior, so take care if you use this where antipopes are possible.

label: Top religious subordinate
summary: Each member of the faith's religious hierarchy on the first level under the head of faith.
details: Works on a faith. Only the first level is included, unlike the full hierarchy list. Challengers (antipopes) count as subordinates of the top superior, so take care. The vanilla files do not use it.

label: Any child is false
summary: Checks whether at least one of the conditions inside is false.
details: This is not a list of things. The game documents only the trigger form `any_false`, which acts like a logical NAND: it is true unless every condition inside is true. The input shows no other form and no vanilla use.

label: Foreign court guest
summary: Each guest who is visiting the character's court from another court.
details: Works on a character. Unlike pool guests, these guests have a liege. Vanilla uses it to collect them into a list, find a ward, and check conditions such as age and culture.

label: Former concubine
summary: Each former concubine of the character.
details: Works on a character. The game's documentation says the list is not persisted past death, without saying whose death. Vanilla uses the trigger form to check whether a saved mother is among them, with `even_if_dead = yes` also seen there.

fields.name: even_if_dead
fields.text: Vanilla writes it with yes when the people it looks for may be dead.

label: Former concubinist
summary: Each character who used to have the character as their concubine.
details: Works on a character. The game's documentation says the list is not persisted past death, without saying whose death. Vanilla uses the trigger form to check whether a saved mother is among them, with `even_if_dead = yes` also seen there.

fields.name: even_if_dead
fields.text: Vanilla writes it with yes when the people it looks for may be dead.

label: Former spouse
summary: Each former spouse of the character.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla also looks at dead former spouses (for example by their death reason), writing `even_if_dead = yes` for that.

fields.name: even_if_dead
fields.text: Vanilla writes it with yes when the people it looks for may be dead.

label: Future route province
summary: Each province on the route of the travel plan.
details: Works on a travel plan. The key name suggests only the part of the route still ahead, but the game's documentation does not say so. Vanilla uses the trigger form to count them, to check terrain, and to check whether the destination of a task is among them.

label: General councillor
summary: Each councillor of the character whose job is not tied to one skill.
details: Works on a character. The vanilla files do not use it.

label: Geographical region
summary: Each geographical region defined in the game.
details: It needs no surrounding scope. Vanilla uses it only to pick a random region and save it.

label: Government type
summary: Each government type defined in the game.
details: It runs over the definitions (feudal, clan and so on), not over rulers, and needs no surrounding scope. The vanilla files do not use it.

label: Grandchild
summary: Each grandchild of the character.
details: Works on a character. The vanilla files do not use it.
